questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My personal ties to Egypt, and in particular to Cairo

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: would've liked more social interaction, so it was fine but i could maybe have gotten more out of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: i honestly dont remember.. but Egypt can sometimes be notorious for "learning by doing", although there's often facebook groups for stuff or if you have friends to ask they are usually helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: i dont really remember. I think it was mostly upon request that we had visas taken care of and such.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: middle-ground, i dont really have an opinion here.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, I found an apartment in the Maadi area of Cairo through what was then called "OLX" but since then has changed name to "Dubizzle"

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: finding landlords that aren't annoying to deal with can be a challenge sometimes. I was lucky during this stay however.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i dont have any opinion on this

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it was pretty straight forward since it was lining up with our university's curriculum.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: it has been too long, i have happily forgotten haha. but i remember that since it was one of the places for mandatory stays - the university was aware of what was required regarding the cooperation with our university, so i believe we received everything by mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: we had pretty close contact with the faculty director and the secretary office was right around the corner too.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As the stay was mandatory, that part was already laid out before us.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont really have any. Maybe if you are in doubt, ask them to send you documents or inquire them by mail.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty good. A little disorganized but the staff had just been rotated so most of them were pretty new i think. But it was fine.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Adequate for 3rd semester. Especially the standard arabic could challenge us.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: we were a small team so it was completely classroom oriented, and a huge focus on us individually.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Standard Arabic (media + literature or poetry), Egyptian arabic

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i dont know, i assume the same ones?

questions.answer: i dont remember, its been a while. But Egypt is pretty cheap - even now with their inflation, so you can easily live off of SU.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: None of them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didnt really have any expectations and as such no requirements.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont remember. But i did get to talk a lot with the Egyptian students at the faculty who were studying German.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Talk with the locals, see the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Find a hobby or something you enjoy doing in Denmark as well and seek it out.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I mean I have been used to Egypt for a while, so for me it was pretty straight forward. But it can be a culture shock the first time.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just hang around campus, they will find you haha.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I dont like the Egyptian gender-social customs very much. The arab world in general, but the "over the shoulder"-surveillance feels particularly apparent in Egypt.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality and social warmth/outgoing nature of Egyptians.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find some egyptian tv shows or literature depending on what you prefer and watch/read them. I especially recommend watching tv shows on Shahid (a streaming service).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Well, sort of.. If you want to communicate naturally in arabic - focus on the dialect. In which case like i said above, watch tv shows and try to talk with locals. It will make it easier for you to get around as well if you can communicate a little with them, and they are very happy to hear you speak even a little bit of broken egyptian.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I had a friend from Algeria visit me and we toured Egypt together. 
If you want to visit other cities such as Alexandria or Port Said, you can take GoBus from downtown, not so far from Talaat Harb Square

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Its more my personal life, but loneliness probably.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: yes - remember to bring foreign currency (USD or Euro) for the student visa, in addition to the entry-visa (25 USD or so). Its difficult to get hold of foreign currency once you're inside the country other than WesternUnion, and make sure to get the currency *before* your initial visa runs out because they wont accept you otherwise.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
